passages.text: Meanwhile, Boaz went to the gate and sat down there. Soon the kinsman-redeemer of whom he had spoken came along, and Boaz said, “Come over here, my friend, and sit down.” So he went over and sat down.
passages.sermon:
Boaz was a respected man in Bethlehem.
Boaz went up to the city gate.
He sat down at the gate.
The city gate was a place for important meetings.
The kinsman-redeemer came by.
This was the man Boaz had spoken about before.
Boaz saw the kinsman-redeemer.
Boaz called to him.
Boaz said, “Come over here, my friend.
Sit down.”
The kinsman-redeemer came over.
He sat down with Boaz.
passages.original: וּבֹ֨עַז עָלָ֣ה הַשַּׁעַר֮ וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב שָׁם֒ וְהִנֵּ֨ה הַגֹּאֵ֤ל עֹבֵר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּר־ בֹּ֔עַז וַיֹּ֛אמֶר ס֥וּרָה שְׁבָה־ פֹּ֖ה פְּלֹנִ֣י אַלְמֹנִ֑י וַיָּ֖סַר וַיֵּשֵֽׁב׃

passages.text: Then Boaz took ten of the elders of the city and said, “Sit here,” and they did so.
passages.sermon:
Boaz was a respected man in Bethlehem.
He wanted to settle an important matter.
Boaz chose ten elders from the city.
These elders were leaders and witnesses in the community.
Boaz spoke to the ten elders.
He said, “Sit here.”
The ten elders sat down.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֞ח עֲשָׂרָ֧ה אֲנָשִׁ֛ים מִזִּקְנֵ֥י הָעִ֖יר וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁבוּ־ פֹ֑ה וַיֵּשֵֽׁבוּ׃

passages.text: And he said to the kinsman-redeemer, “Naomi, who has returned from the land of Moab, is selling the piece of land that belonged to our brother Elimelech.
passages.sermon:
Boaz spoke to the kinsman-redeemer.
Naomi is a widow.
Naomi returned from the land of Moab.
Naomi is selling a piece of land.
This land belonged to Elimelech.
Elimelech was our relative.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לַגֹּאֵ֔ל חֶלְקַת֙ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְאָחִ֖ינוּ לֶאֱלִימֶ֑לֶךְ מָכְרָ֣ה נָעֳמִ֔י הַשָּׁ֖בָה מִשְּׂדֵ֥ה מוֹאָֽב׃

passages.text: I thought I should inform you that you may buy it back in the presence of those seated here and in the presence of the elders of my people. If you want to redeem it, do so. But if you will not redeem it, tell me so I may know, because there is no one but you to redeem it, and I am next after you.” “I will redeem it,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
Boaz spoke to the kinsman-redeemer.
Boaz said, "You may buy the land."
The land belonged to Elimelech.
Naomi is selling the land.
We are here with the elders of my people.
The elders and others are sitting here.
If you want to redeem the land, do it.
If you do not want to redeem it, tell me.
I need to know your answer.
No one else can redeem it except you.
I am next after you.
The kinsman-redeemer answered.
He said, "I will redeem it."
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֨י אָמַ֜רְתִּי אֶגְלֶ֧ה אָזְנְךָ֣ לֵאמֹ֗ר קְ֠נֵה נֶ֥גֶד הַֽיֹּשְׁבִים֮ וְנֶ֣גֶד זִקְנֵ֣י עַמִּי֒ אִם־ תִּגְאַל֙ גְּאָ֔ל וְאִם־ לֹ֨א יִגְאַ֜ל הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י וְאֵדַע כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין זוּלָֽתְךָ֙ לִגְא֔וֹל וְאָנֹכִ֖י אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָנֹכִ֥י אֶגְאָֽל׃

passages.text: Then Boaz said, “On the day you buy the land from Naomi and also from Ruth the Moabitess, you must also acquire the widow of the deceased in order to raise up the name of the deceased on his inheritance.”
passages.sermon:
Boaz spoke to the kinsman-redeemer.
Boaz was a relative of Naomi and Ruth.
Boaz said, "You will buy the field from Naomi."
Naomi returned from Moab.
The field belonged to Elimelech, Naomi’s late husband.
You will also acquire Ruth the Moabitess.
Ruth is the widow of the deceased.
You must take Ruth as part of the purchase.
You must do this to raise up the name of the deceased.
You will preserve the inheritance of the dead man.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר בֹּ֔עַז בְּיוֹם־ קְנוֹתְךָ֥ הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה מִיַּ֣ד נָעֳמִ֑י וּ֠מֵאֵת ר֣וּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּ֤ה אֵֽשֶׁת־ הַמֵּת֙ קָנִיתִי לְהָקִ֥ים שֵׁם־ הַמֵּ֖ת עַל־ נַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The kinsman-redeemer replied, “I cannot redeem it myself, or I would jeopardize my own inheritance. Take my right of redemption, because I cannot redeem it.”
passages.sermon:
The kinsman-redeemer spoke.
He said, “I cannot redeem it for myself.
If I redeem it, I might harm my own inheritance.
You may redeem it instead of me.
I give you my right of redemption.
I cannot redeem it.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַגֹּאֵ֗ל לֹ֤א אוּכַל֙ לִגְאוֹל לִ֔י פֶּן־ אַשְׁחִ֖ית אֶת־ נַחֲלָתִ֑י גְּאַל־ לְךָ֤ אַתָּה֙ אֶת־ גְּאֻלָּתִ֔י כִּ֥י לֹא־ אוּכַ֖ל לִגְאֹֽל׃

passages.text: Now in former times in Israel, concerning the redemption or exchange of property, to make any matter legally binding a man would remove his sandal and give it to the other party, and this was a confirmation in Israel.
passages.sermon:
In ancient Israel, people had a custom for legal agreements.
This custom applied to redeeming or exchanging property.
To make an agreement binding, a man would take off his sandal.
He would give his sandal to the other person.
This act served as a confirmation in Israel.
passages.original: וְזֹאת֩ לְפָנִ֨ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל עַל־ הַגְּאוּלָּ֤ה וְעַל־ הַתְּמוּרָה֙ לְקַיֵּ֣ם כָּל־ דָּבָ֔ר שָׁלַ֥ף אִ֛ישׁ נַעֲל֖וֹ וְנָתַ֣ן לְרֵעֵ֑הוּ וְזֹ֥את הַתְּעוּדָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: So the kinsman-redeemer removed his sandal and said to Boaz, “Buy it for yourself.”
passages.sermon:
The kinsman-redeemer spoke to Boaz.
He said, “Buy it for yourself.”
The kinsman-redeemer took off his sandal.
He gave his sandal to Boaz.
This act showed that Boaz could buy the property.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר הַגֹּאֵ֛ל לְבֹ֖עַז קְנֵה־ לָ֑ךְ וַיִּשְׁלֹ֖ף נַעֲלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: At this, Boaz said to the elders and all the people, “You are witnesses today that I am buying from Naomi all that belonged to Elimelech, Chilion, and Mahlon.
passages.sermon:
Boaz spoke to the elders and to all the people.
Boaz said, “You are witnesses today.
I am buying everything that belonged to Elimelech.
I am also buying everything that belonged to Chilion and Mahlon.
I am buying these things from Naomi.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ בֹּ֨עַז לַזְּקֵנִ֜ים וְכָל־ הָעָ֗ם עֵדִ֤ים אַתֶּם֙ הַיּ֔וֹם כִּ֤י קָנִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֶֽאֱלִימֶ֔לֶךְ וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְכִלְי֖וֹן וּמַחְל֑וֹן מִיַּ֖ד נָעֳמִֽי׃

passages.text: Moreover, I have acquired Ruth the Moabitess, Mahlon’s widow, as my wife, to raise up the name of the deceased through his inheritance, so that his name will not disappear from among his brothers or from the gate of his home. You are witnesses today.”
passages.sermon:
Boaz spoke to the elders and all the people.
Boaz said he had acquired Ruth as his wife.
Ruth is a Moabite woman.
Ruth was the wife of Mahlon.
Boaz took Ruth to be his wife.
Boaz did this to preserve the name of the dead.
The dead man is Mahlon.
Boaz wanted Mahlon's name to remain with his inheritance.
Boaz did not want Mahlon's name to disappear from among his brothers.
Boaz did not want Mahlon's name to be lost from the gate of his home.
Boaz declared that the elders and all the people were witnesses that day.
passages.original: וְגַ֣ם אֶת־ ר֣וּת הַמֹּאֲבִיָּה֩ אֵ֨שֶׁת מַחְל֜וֹן קָנִ֧יתִי לִ֣י לְאִשָּׁ֗ה לְהָקִ֤ים שֵׁם־ הַמֵּת֙ עַל־ נַ֣חֲלָת֔וֹ וְלֹא־ יִכָּרֵ֧ת שֵׁם־ הַמֵּ֛ת מֵעִ֥ם אֶחָ֖יו וּמִשַּׁ֣עַר מְקוֹמ֑וֹ עֵדִ֥ים אַתֶּ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: “We are witnesses,” said the elders and all the people at the gate. “May the LORD make the woman entering your home like Rachel and Leah, who together built up the house of Israel. May you be prosperous in Ephrathah and famous in Bethlehem.
passages.sermon:
The elders stood at the gate.
All the people stood with them.
They said, “We are witnesses.”
They spoke to Boaz.
They said, “May the LORD bless the woman who comes into your house.”
They asked God to make her like Rachel and Leah.
Rachel and Leah built up the house of Israel together.
They asked God to give Boaz strength in Ephrathah.
They asked that Boaz would have a good name in Bethlehem.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ כָּל־ הָעָ֧ם אֲשֶׁר־ בַּשַּׁ֛עַר וְהַזְּקֵנִ֖ים עֵדִ֑ים יִתֵּן֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֶֽת־ הָאִשָּׁ֜ה הַבָּאָ֣ה אֶל־ בֵּיתֶ֗ךָ כְּרָחֵ֤ל׀ וּכְלֵאָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּנ֤וּ שְׁתֵּיהֶם֙ אֶת־ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַעֲשֵׂה־ חַ֣יִל בְּאֶפְרָ֔תָה וּקְרָא־ שֵׁ֖ם בְּבֵ֥ית לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: And may your house become like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, because of the offspring the LORD will give you by this young woman.”
passages.sermon:
Perez was the son of Judah and Tamar.
Perez’s family became strong and important in Israel.
May your house become like the house of Perez.
May God give you children by this young woman.
May your family grow and be blessed because of these children.
passages.original: וִיהִ֤י בֵֽיתְךָ֙ כְּבֵ֣ית פֶּ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־ יָלְדָ֥ה תָמָ֖ר לִֽיהוּדָ֑ה מִן־ הַזֶּ֗רַע אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִתֵּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ מִן־ הַֽנַּעֲרָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. And when he had relations with her, the LORD enabled her to conceive, and she gave birth to a son.
passages.sermon:
Boaz took Ruth as his wife.
Ruth became Boaz’s wife.
Boaz had relations with Ruth.
The LORD enabled Ruth to conceive.
Ruth gave birth to a son.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֨ח בֹּ֤עַז אֶת־ רוּת֙ וַתְּהִי־ ל֣וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א אֵלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה לָ֛הּ הֵרָי֖וֹן וַתֵּ֥לֶד בֵּֽן׃

passages.text: Then the women said to Naomi, “Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you this day without a kinsman-redeemer. May his name become famous in Israel.
passages.sermon:
Naomi was an Israelite woman.
Women spoke to Naomi.
They said, "Blessed be the LORD."
The LORD did not leave you without a kinsman-redeemer today.
May his name become famous in Israel.
passages.original: וַתֹּאמַ֤רְנָה הַנָּשִׁים֙ אֶֽל־ נָעֳמִ֔י בָּר֣וּךְ יְהוָ֔ה אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹ֣א הִשְׁבִּ֥ית לָ֛ךְ גֹּאֵ֖ל הַיּ֑וֹם וְיִקָּרֵ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: He will renew your life and sustain you in your old age. For your daughter-in-law, who loves you and is better to you than seven sons, has given him birth.”
passages.sermon:
Naomi was an older woman.
She had a daughter-in-law named Ruth.
Ruth loved Naomi.
Ruth was better to Naomi than seven sons.
Ruth gave birth to a son.
This son would renew Naomi’s life.
This son would take care of Naomi in her old age.
passages.original: וְהָ֤יָה לָךְ֙ לְמֵשִׁ֣יב נֶ֔פֶשׁ וּלְכַלְכֵּ֖ל אֶת־ שֵׂיבָתֵ֑ךְ כִּ֣י כַלָּתֵ֤ךְ אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־ אֲהֵבַ֙תֶךְ֙ יְלָדַ֔תּוּ אֲשֶׁר־ הִיא֙ ט֣וֹבָה לָ֔ךְ מִשִּׁבְעָ֖ה בָּנִֽים׃

passages.text: And Naomi took the child, placed him on her lap, and became a nurse to him.
passages.sermon:
Naomi was an older woman from Bethlehem.
Naomi took the child.
She placed the child on her lap.
Naomi became a nurse to the child.
passages.original: וַתִּקַּ֨ח נָעֳמִ֤י אֶת־ הַיֶּ֙לֶד֙ וַתְּשִׁתֵ֣הוּ בְחֵיקָ֔הּ וַתְּהִי־ ל֖וֹ לְאֹמֶֽנֶת׃

passages.text: The neighbor women said, “A son has been born to Naomi,” and they named him Obed. He became the father of Jesse, the father of David.
passages.sermon:
The neighbor women spoke.
They said a son was born to Naomi.
The women gave the child a name.
They named him Obed.
Obed became the father of Jesse.
Jesse became the father of David.
passages.original: וַתִּקְרֶאנָה֩ ל֨וֹ הַשְּׁכֵנ֥וֹת שֵׁם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יֻלַּד־ בֵּ֖ן לְנָעֳמִ֑י וַתִּקְרֶ֤אנָֽה שְׁמוֹ֙ עוֹבֵ֔ד ה֥וּא אֲבִי־ יִשַׁ֖י אֲבִ֥י דָוִֽד׃פ

passages.text: Now these are the generations of Perez: Perez was the father of Hezron, Hezron was the father of Ram, Ram was the father of Amminadab, Amminadab was the father of Nahshon, Nahshon was the father of Salmon, Salmon was the father of Boaz, Boaz was the father of Obed, Obed was the father of Jesse, and Jesse was the father of David.
passages.sermon:
Perez was an ancestor of King David.
Perez had a son named Hezron.
Hezron had a son named Ram.
Ram had a son named Amminadab.
Amminadab had a son named Nahshon.
Nahshon had a son named Salmon.
Salmon had a son named Boaz.
Boaz had a son named Obed.
Obed had a son named Jesse.
Jesse had a son named David.
passages.original: וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ תּוֹלְד֣וֹת פָּ֔רֶץ פֶּ֖רֶץ הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־ חֶצְרֽוֹן׃ וְחֶצְרוֹן֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־ רָ֔ם וְרָ֖ם הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־ עַמִּֽינָדָֽב׃ וְעַמִּֽינָדָב֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־ נַחְשׁ֔וֹן וְנַחְשׁ֖וֹן הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־ שַׂלְמָֽה׃ וְשַׂלְמוֹן֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־ בֹּ֔עַז וּבֹ֖עַז הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־ עוֹבֵֽד׃ וְעֹבֵד֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־ יִשָׁ֔י וְיִשַׁ֖י הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־ דָּוִֽד׃
